prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The researchers created a small, modular device that can record from up to 128 channels at once.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The device measures electrical signals with very low background noise, around 3.0 microvolts for fast spikes and 2.6 microvolts for slower brain waves.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The part of the device that sits on the animal's head weighs just 1.3 grams for a 64-channel module.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The system can send data either wirelessly or through a wire, depending on the experiment.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The device was tested in living animals to confirm it could accurately record both slow brain waves and individual neuron spikes.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study recorded brain activity from two different areas, the nucleus accumbens and the dorsal CA1, in five mice at the same time.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The recordings showed that the two brain regions were synchronized at low frequencies between 0.5 and 5 Hz.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Individual neuron spikes in the dorsal CA1 were closely timed to the slow rhythmic waves in the nucleus accumbens.
facts.subject: animals
